s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute painful skin lesion with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful, warm, and nodular skin lesion
History of similar lesion that resolved spontaneously
Presence of Gram-negative coccobacilli on Gram stain
key_facts: 34-year-old breastfeeding woman
Subacute onset of skin lesion
Lesion located between neck and breast
Lesion measures approximately 3 × 4 cm
Patient has a history of travel to East-Turkish region
Patient has a VP shunt
Leukocyte count is elevated at 11.15 × 10⁹/L
C-reactive protein is elevated at 15 mg/L
Ultrasound examination shows inflammatory subcutaneous collection
Aspirate microscopy shows amorphous debris and neutrophil granulocytes
Gram staining shows Gram-negative coccobacilli
Culture is positive for B. melitensis biovar 3

shortlist.label: Brucellosis
shortlist.why_kept: Culture is positive for B. melitensis biovar 3

shortlist.label: Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Ultrasound examination shows inflammatory subcutaneous collection

shortlist.label: Cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated leukocyte count and C-reactive protein with subacute onset of skin lesion

shortlist.label: Infected epidermal cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous collection with amorphous debris and neutrophil granulocytes on aspirate microscopy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of travel to an East-Turkish region, a known endemic area for Brucellosis, combined with the culture positive for B. melitensis biovar 3, strongly supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has an inflammatory subcutaneous collection, the presence of B. melitensis biovar 3 suggests a specific infectious cause

rejected.label: Cellulitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and lab results do not fully align with typical cellulitis, and the culture results point to a specific infection

rejected.label: Infected epidermal cyst
rejected.why: There is no mention of a cyst, and the patient's symptoms and lab results suggest a more systemic infection

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: The Gram stain and culture results do not support Actinomycosis, which typically shows Gram-positive filamentous bacteria
